mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT at t-0w signals a broad activity shock that suppresses discretionary shopping with a short lag. If this shock persists for two to four weeks, RETAIL_REC should remain below its prior four-week average.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay near the t-0w levels for the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 20 percentage points while WORKPLACES remains below -40, households are staying home more and replacing shopping trips with home-based activity, which lowers RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 20 while WORKPLACES is below -40
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 20 and WORKPLACES stays below -40 for a full week but RETAIL_REC does not fall in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized downturn in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and PARKS indicates a mobility clampdown that reduces cross-district shopping access. Under that regime, retail-and-recreation mobility should decline over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and PARKS all remain depressed but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the previous four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after an abrupt trough is a proxy for improved weather or seasonal outdoor demand, which tends to pull people away from indoor retail in the following two weeks. RETAIL_REC should therefore weaken after PARKS recovers from a sharp weekly drop.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -40 then turns upward
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds above -35 for two weeks after the t-0w trough and RETAIL_REC still rises relative to the last four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling GROCERY_PHARM and falling WORKPLACES indicates reduced trip chaining and fewer errand-linked shopping visits. That should translate into lower retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES remain suppressed but RETAIL_REC does not stay below its last-four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises, consumers are shifting toward home-centered routines that reduce spontaneous shopping trips. This should depress RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops > 5 points week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL rises
evidence_refs: fact:t-2w to t-1w and t-1w to t-0w show RESIDENTIAL rising while TRANSIT remains weak
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL rises but RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside a collapse in PARKS is consistent with localized precautionary behavior or access limits that shift trips toward essentials and away from discretionary venues. RETAIL_REC should fall over the next one to four weeks under that condition.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while PARKS falls below -40
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises and PARKS stays below -40 but RETAIL_REC does not weaken over the following month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The abrupt simultaneous declines in RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, and TRANSIT at t-0w imply a fresh shock rather than a gradual trend. If this is a one-week interruption, RETAIL_REC should partially rebound within four weeks; if the decline persists, the hypothesis fails.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls more than 25 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC remains near or below -60 for four weeks after the t-0w drop, with no rebound in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, the hypothesis is rejected.
